review.summary: Phase 3 is substantially implemented with unusually strong, genuinely independent evidence. Native models (183k generated lines, 14 reproducible outputs), a data-driven Zod interpreter covering all 13,018 frozen nodes, 69 source-hash-pinned semantic bindings, the content builder, all four scanner methods, and representative OAuth read / SSE stream / binary download clients are all present and tested. Verification is real, not claimed: 60,271 oracle JSON cases compared in both modes against actual frozen Zod execution, 27,216 typed round-trips in a separate consumer crate, 132 Rust tests plus doctest across 1.88.0/1.99.0 and default/minimal/all/json-unification, with exact recorded commands, exit codes and stdout. Redaction, presence semantics (Optional/Nullable/Patch), bounded validation, no-replay on paid POST/stream paths, destination/plane isolation and traversal rejection are all concretely tested. The blocking gap is wire-contract completeness in the representative slice: the frozen baseline sends `service-name: api` and a `PAN-AIRS/...` User-Agent on every request — the latter pinned by a frozen fixture that records 400 failures on tenants requiring it — and the Rust clients send neither, with no recorded deliberate-difference rationale. The scan wire test asserts only a header subset, so it could not detect this. Two smaller behavioral deviations (typed SSE aborting on empty-data frames the baseline skips; `Intersection` demanding byte-identical halves) and one doc claim unsupported by the cited tests ("uncertain outcomes") also need resolution. Everything else is at or above the 9 bar; fixing the header omission plus tightening the wire assertions should get this over the threshold quickly.

findings.description: The SDK never sends the baseline's mandatory `service-name: api` request header. The frozen source sets it on every request (.local/typescript/src/http/request.ts:93), and this repository's own frozen fixture pins it with an explicit regression note: "AIRS DLP GET-by-id endpoints return 400 on tenants whose downstream services require the `service-name: api` header" (contracts/fixtures/typescript/test/http/request.spec.ts:171-189). No Rust code path adds it (grep for `service-name` across crates/ and docs/ returns nothing), it is not in `forbidden_header` (engine.rs:106), and no document records it as a deliberate difference. This affects all four scan operations, the management read and both gateway operations implemented in this phase, and is exactly the kind of transport-contract deviation phase 3's wire-check criterion is meant to catch.
findings.required_fix: Add `service-name: api` to the SDK-owned default header set in request assembly (engine.rs `send_bytes`/`send_stream`, so it applies regardless of injected transport), assert it in the scan/management/gateway wire tests, and record it in docs/SCANNING.md plus the operation contract ledger. If omission is intended, document the rationale and the tenant-failure risk explicitly as an accepted difference.

findings.description: The baseline sets `User-Agent: PAN-AIRS/<version>-typescript-sdk` on every request and pins it with a frozen test (`sets User-Agent on every request`, contracts/fixtures/typescript/test/http/request.spec.ts:155-169). Rust sets `scm-sdk/0.1.0` only inside the optional reqwest adapter builder, so a caller-supplied `Transport` (the documented integration point, and the one used by every test in this phase) transmits no SDK User-Agent at all. No document records this difference.
findings.required_fix: Set an SDK-owned User-Agent header during request assembly rather than only in the reqwest adapter, assert it in the wire tests, and record the chosen value as a documented deliberate difference from the baseline string in docs/SCANNING.md or docs/FOUNDATION.md.

findings.description: An SSE frame whose only data line is empty yields a raw event (`has_data` is set true for an empty value at finish_line:369-374, and the event is emitted at 350). The baseline skips such frames entirely (`if (!payload) continue;`, .local/typescript/src/http/event-stream.ts:136). In the typed path this is not benign: ContractStream calls `event.json()` (streaming.rs:58), which fails on empty data, closes the stream and latches a Decode failure — so a server keep-alive `data:` line terminates a billable chat-completion stream that the frozen SDK tolerates. docs/STREAMING.md:46-47 records the raw-event behavior but presents the resulting typed decode error as acceptable rather than as a tolerated-frame regression.
findings.required_fix: Skip empty-data frames in the typed ContractStream path (or make it an explicit policy knob matching the baseline default), and add a test with an interleaved empty-data keep-alive frame proving the typed stream survives and still reaches its terminal.

findings.description: `assert_wire` checks only that specific headers are present/absent (x-pan-token, authorization, x-payload-hash, content-type) and never asserts the complete header name set. The same is true of `assert_runtime_wire` (tests/representative_clients.rs:314-337) and the management test (line 206-213). Because of this, the two missing baseline default headers above pass all recorded wire checks, which weakens the "HMAC scan wire checks" acceptance evidence for this phase.
findings.required_fix: Assert the exact sorted set of transmitted header names (not just selected ones) in the scan, management and gateway wire tests, so any added or missing SDK-owned header is caught by the gate.

findings.description: The document states the "Six independent tests exercise all four frozen wire fixtures, literal HMAC computation, invalid-input rejection, uncertain outcomes, and safe formatting." The six tests in crates/scm-sdk/tests/scan_contracts.rs contain no reference to RemoteOutcome or remote_outcome (verified by grep: zero matches) and no ambiguous-failure case; uncertain-outcome behavior is tested generically in engine::tests, not in the cited scan suite. Phase gating requires evidence claims to match the artifacts they cite.
findings.required_fix: Either add a scan test that asserts RemoteOutcome::Unknown on an ambiguous transport/post-send failure for sync_scan/async_scan, or correct docs/SCANNING.md to attribute uncertain-outcome evidence to the engine test suite.

findings.description: `Intersection::new` and its Serialize impl require the left and right halves to serialize to byte-identical JSON, which is stricter than Zod's intersection semantics (the validator itself merges both outputs, validation.rs:637-658). Any intersection where one side strips fields the other retains would be rejected or fail to serialize. This difference is not recorded in docs/MODELS.md, and coverage rests only on the specimens the oracle happened to generate.
findings.required_fix: Align the typed Intersection representation with the validator's merge semantics (or document the stricter rule in docs/MODELS.md) and add a direct test for an intersection whose halves have differing normalized representations.

findings.description: The `finite_json` and `finite_json_object` arms of `apply` are unreachable: `walk` intercepts both bindings before calling `apply` (validation.rs:566-575) and uses the bounded, depth-ticked `check_finite_json`. The dead arms call `safe_json` (line 663), which recurses with no depth or work budget. Harmless today, but it is an unbudgeted recursive path one refactor away from being reachable.
findings.required_fix: Remove the unreachable `finite_json`/`finite_json_object` arms from `apply` and the now-unused `safe_json` helper, or route them through the bounded `check_finite_json` implementation.

findings.description: The recorded feature matrix covers only default, minimal, all and json-unification. No check builds a single product feature in isolation (for example `--features management` or `--features gateway` alone), yet engine.rs gates AuthKind variants, require_auth arms and contract helpers per feature (engine.rs:150-157, 323-338, 406). A single-feature consumer build is plausible for this crate's additive feature design but is currently unverified.
findings.required_fix: Add one isolated single-product feature configuration (for example `--no-default-features --features management`) to the phase check matrix, or state in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md that only default/minimal/all combinations are supported and verified.

findings.description: Public rustdoc contains run-together text: "Submit1–20objects" (missing spaces). The same artifact appears in docs prose ("Phase3", "Phase8" in docs/SCANNING.md:42 and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:33, "expiry literal7 accepted30" in tools/generate_models.py:746). This ships in generated API documentation.
findings.required_fix: Fix the spacing in the public doc comment and the equivalent occurrences in docs/SCANNING.md and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-03.json records 20 commands matching tools/check_phase.py:47-66 exactly, all exit_code 0, source_sha256 ab82ef82...e9a4e, source_unchanged true, passed true.

docs/checks/phase-03-rust-1.99.0-all.json contains actual cargo stdout: 107 unit tests, 14 representative_clients, 6 scan_contracts, 5 schema_contracts, 1 doctest, all passing; fmt/check/clippy -D warnings/test/doc all exit 0 on x86_64-unknown-linux-musl with rustc 1.99.0. Equivalent reports exist for 1.88.0 default/minimal/all, 1.99.0 default/minimal, and 1.99.0 json-unification (serde_json/arbitrary_precision).

tools/schema-oracle.mts reconstructs the frozen tree, deletes all environment variables, forbids fetch/WebSocket, imports the frozen Zod modules and emits expectations from real safeParse; crates/scm-sdk/tests/schema_contracts.rs:74-128 compares all 60,271 jsonCases in both Request and Response modes and asserts the checked count equals counts.jsonCases.

Recorded oracle counts: publicSchemaExports 1086, uniqueRoots 1085, jsonCoveredRoots 1080, requiresNativeInput 5 (all Gateway Blob-input schemas), unresolvedValidSpecimens [], rootsWithoutJsonRejection [], acceptedJsonCases 12956, rejectedJsonCases 47315.

generate_models.py --verify-fixtures output: {"expiryLiteralIdentityChecks":6,"failures":0,"nativeOnlySchemas":5,"publicSchemas":1086,"typedCases":27216,"typedSchemas":1081} from a separate crate (.local/typed-model-oracle) depending only on scm-sdk with features=["models"].

tools/generate_validation.py verifies each of the 69 semantic bindings against a pinned source-expression sha256, fails on any unrecognized semantic, asserts the inventory count is exactly 69, and byte-compares both the public ledger and the runtime registry under --check; every binding name present in contracts/native-semantics.json is handled by validation.rs::apply (native_* are deliberately rejected for JSON input).

schema_graph.json contains no "type":"preprocess" effect nodes, so validation.rs applying all ZodEffects after the core parse (effects collected then reversed, validation.rs:328-373 and 566-579) preserves source ordering.

contracts/native-models.json: 264 deferred_client_adapter rows, all with owningPhase 4-7 (grep for "owningPhase": 3 returns no matches), and the generator raises if any known source model lacks an adapter (generate_models.py:788-790) - so no scan-family model export is deferred out of this phase.

Scan parity against .local/typescript: paths /v1/scan/sync/request, /v1/scan/async/request, /v1/scan/results, /v1/scan/reports; region endpoints service/service-de/service-in/service-sg; MAX_CONTENT_* 2 MiB/2 MiB/100 MiB; 5 scan ids, 5 report ids, 20 batch objects; retry cap 5 (constants.ts:24-75 vs scanner.rs:19-26,126,178-192, content.rs:6-7, config.rs:313,368-371).

Auth header parity confirmed: .local/typescript/src/http/auth/api-key.ts sets x-pan-token, Authorization: Bearer, and x-payload-hash only when a body exists; tests/scan_contracts.rs:126-147 asserts the same, with independently computed HMAC-SHA256 over the exact transmitted bytes and is_sensitive() on all three.

Gap evidence: .local/typescript/src/http/request.ts:91-95 sets 'User-Agent' and 'service-name': 'api' on every request; contracts/fixtures/typescript/test/http/request.spec.ts:155-189 pins both with a #162 regression note about 400 responses; grep for service-name across crates/ returns zero matches and across docs/ returns zero matches; transport.rs:154 is the only user_agent occurrence and lives inside the optional reqwest adapter.

SSE divergence evidence: .local/typescript/src/http/event-stream.ts:136 (`if (!payload) continue;`) versus sse.rs:369-374 setting has_data for an empty value and sse.rs:350 emitting the event, with streaming.rs:58 then failing json decoding and latching the failure.

Security properties verified in code and covered by named passing tests: Debug redaction on all wrappers/models/content/secrets (data.rs, support.rs, content.rs:215-224); bounded validation with iterative preflight and non-recursive discard of overdeep input (validation.rs:212-256); serialize depth cap 128 and byte-bounded writer (engine.rs:808-868); replay_safe false for all POSTs (engine.rs:36-53); plane isolation via require_auth (engine.rs:324-338, test product_clients_reject_credentials_from_the_other_plane_before_network); permit/body release on drop, close, terminal and failure (sse.rs:401-405, tests stream_drop_before_or_after_iteration_releases_the_concurrency_permit and oversized_binary_download_is_unknown_and_releases_its_body_and_permit).

#![forbid(unsafe_code)] at lib.rs:5; no todo!/unimplemented! in non-test library code; docs/DEPENDENCIES.md:16-31 records the newly added regex, ryu-js and time dependencies with versions, MSRV and licenses, and the phase-2 advisory items (combined header bounds engine.rs:124-133, 403/x-opa-decision refresh engine.rs:748-752, TLS rootstore review DEPENDENCIES.md:43-61) are all present in the reviewed source.
limitations: Read-only review: I executed nothing. I could not recompute the source fingerprint, so I cannot independently confirm that the working tree still hashes to ab82ef8269ad98d74089305d32ea4100cf4a37e1c0e853fc08e727b0f43e9a4e or that docs/checks/phase-03.json hashes to the stated 43c8e635... value; I verified internal consistency of the recorded reports instead.

Recorded check reports are trusted as faithful transcripts of the runs. The phase-3 test stdout is detailed and internally consistent (test names match the source files I read), but the gate's own documentation notes these hashes detect staleness rather than authenticate the process.

I did not read all 183,247 lines of crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs. I inspected representative generated types (ScanRequest, ScanRequestContentsInner) and relied on the byte-exact generator --check plus the 27,216-case typed oracle for the remainder.

No live service acceptance exists or was attempted; all evidence is offline and credential-free. Live scan/management/gateway qualification is deferred to phase 8 per docs/phase-status.json, and I treated it as out of scope.

The response-widening expectations in contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json come from a policy reimplementation layered over real Zod execution (tools/schema-oracle.mts:215-250), not from Zod alone; the request-mode half is unmodified frozen Zod. A systematic error in that documented widening policy would be invisible to the Rust comparison.
I did not inspect credential or tenant-registration files, and did not read anything outside this repository; .local/typescript was inspected only as the permitted frozen nonsecret reference.
Single-feature and non-musl platform behavior is unverified by any recorded evidence, so my assessment of those configurations is based on reading the cfg gates rather than execution.
